releases.body:
Atlantis v0.49.0 v0.49.0 is a breaking release , for three reasons: The Docker images no longer include Terraform or OpenTofu. This was announced in v0.48.0. 12 security advisories are fixed here, and several of those fixes change behavior that existing setups may rely on. v0.47.1 shipped a breaking change without saying so: the shell-injection fix in #6792 . It is listed below so anyone upgrading from v0.47.0 or earlier sees it. Every behavior change is also documented, in a Behavior change note, on the docs page where you would look for that setting. Read Breaking changes before you upgrade. Upgrade checklist Docker images: set --default-tf-version (and --default-tf-distribution opentofu if you use OpenTofu) so Atlantis downloads the binary. If downloads are blocked, mount or copy a binary into the image instead. The image no longer ships one. Upgrading from v0.47.0 or earlier: check workspace names and comment arguments against the v0.47.1 changes below. GitHub / GHES: make sure --gh-hostname matches the host in your repositories' clone URLs. Webhooks whose clone URL is on a different host are now rejected. Server-side repo config: if repos use allow_custom_workflows: true together with allowed_workflows , check that every project's workflow is in the allow-list. Repo configs that used to pass can now be rejected. Project dirs: make sure no project dir is a symlink to somewhere outside the repository. Comment commands: tell users that -out , -generate-config-out , -state , -state-out and -backup are now blocked after -- , and that --blocked-extra-args can no longer unblock anything. Comment -var-file : the allowlist now applies to apply , import and state rm as well as plan . Paths containing .. are refused, and so are repo symlinks that point outside the repository and the allowlist. state rm : if state is in --allow-commands , state rm now has to meet the project's apply_requirements and import_requirements . API: if --api-secret is set, send X-Atlantis-Token on GET /api/locks . Check that /api/plan and /api/apply callers send clean, repo-relative paths[].directory values with no leading / and no globs. Approvals (GitHub, Gitea): apply_requirements: [approved] now uses each reviewer's latest review. On Gitea, dismissed and stale approvals no longer count, and any push that changes the diff makes approvals stale. Apply: plans recorded by v0.49.0 are bound to a hash. A plan file that changes between plan and apply is rejected and has to be re-planned. Breaking changes Docker images The Docker images no longer include Terraform or OpenTofu What changed: the latest , vX.Y.Z and vX.Y.Z-debian images no longer bundle Terraform or OpenTofu binaries, and they set no default Terraform version. This was announced in the v0.48.0 release notes. The -alpine-slim and -debian-slim images from v0.48.0 were the intermediate step toward this and are no longer published . If you pinned one, switch to the unsuffixed, -alpine or -debian tag, which now contain the same thing. If you build the image yourself, use --target alpine or --target debian ; the -slim targets are gone. Why: every advisory against any bundled Terraform or OpenTofu release showed up in scans of the Atlantis image, whether or not you used that version. Atlantis can't own the security lifecycle of those third-party binaries. Who is affected: anyone using the published images who relied on the bundled terraform or tofu binary on PATH , or on the version the image used to set by default. How to tell: the server refuses to start with terraform not found in $PATH. Set --default-tf-version ... . What to do: Set --default-tf-version ( ATLANTIS_DEFAULT_TF_VERSION , or Helm defaultTFVersion ) so Atlantis downloads that version at startup. Repos can still pin their own version with terraform_version . For OpenTofu, also set --default-tf-distribution opentofu (Helm defaultTFDistribution ). If the server can't reach the release hosts, put a binary on PATH yourself: mount one, or build FROM ghcr.io/runatlantis/atlantis and copy one in. Set --tf-download=false so Atlantis uses it and doesn't try to download. See Deployment: image variants . Carried over from v0.47.1 ( #6792 ) v0.47.1 fixed a shell-injection vulnerability ( GHSA-rjh2-4xgw-p2hj ) and changed behavior along the way, but its release notes didn't call that a breaking change. If you are upgrading from v0.47.0 or earlier, these apply to you. Terraform and conftest commands no longer run through a shell What changed: Atlantis used to build Terraform and conftest command lines as strings and run them with sh -c . Commands now run as argument vectors. Each extra_args entry is passed as exactly one argument. Shell operators ( ; , && , | , redirections), globbing and word splitting no longer apply. Environment references such as $WORKSPACE and $DIR are still expanded in operator-configured extra_args , but no longer in arguments typed in a PR comment after -- . For conftest, a policy set path and each extra_args entry are still split on whitespace. Quote a path that contains a space. Who is affected: Workflows whose extra_args relied on shell behavior, for example two flags in one entry, a pipe, a redirection or a glob. Users who passed $VAR references in comment arguments and expected them to expand. What to do: split multi-flag entries into one argument per entry. Move anything that needs a shell into a run step, which still runs with a shell by design. Workspace names are validated everywhere What changed: workspace names from repo atlantis.yaml , the -w comment flag, the Terraform Cloud workspace read from HCL, and the API are validated. A name can't contain / , \ , .. , $ , whitespace or control characters, can't be . , and can't start with - or ~ . Who is affected: projects or comments using such names. A name containing $ never worked, because the shell expanded it. How to tell: repo config validation fails under the workspace key, or the comment is rejected with the offending value and a reason such as cannot contain '/' or '\' . What to do: rename the workspace to one without those characters. Server-side repo config allowed_workflows is now checked for every project ( GHSA-56q6-8vmp-v2qm ) What changed: with allow_custom_workflows: true , a bug stopped the allowed_workflows check at the first project that used a repo-local workflow. Projects after that one were never checked. Now every project is checked. Who is affected: repos with allow_custom_workflows: true , allowed_overrides: [workflow] and a non-empty allowed_workflows , whose atlantis.yaml has a later project naming a server-side workflow that is not in allowed_workflows . How to tell: the repo config fails validation with workflow '' is not allowed for this repo . What to do: add the workflow to the repo's allowed_workflows in the server-side config, or change the project to use an allowed workflow. A project dir that symlinks outside the repository is rejected ( GHSA-9q39-mgw7-5789 ) What changed: Atlantis now follows symlinks before checking that a project directory is inside the clone. Before, the check only looked at the path as written. Who is affected: repos whose project dir (or a parent directory in its path) is a symlink pointing outside the clone. That includes absolute targets and ../ targets that leave the repository. Symlinks that stay inside the repository (for example dir -> modules/x ) still work. How to tell: plan, apply, import and state commands fail with project path traversal detected: ... . A path that cannot be resolved for any other reason (for example a file where a directory is expected) now fails with resolving project path: ... . Before, Atlantis ignored that case. What to do: replace the symlink with a real directory inside the repository, or point it at a target inside the repository. Also changed: a broken dir symlink keeps the existing dir "" does not exist error. If anything other than a regular file (for example a symlink) sits at the plan file path inside the project directory, Atlantis deletes it before planning. Comment commands More Terraform flags are blocked after -- , and --blocked-extra-args now adds to the list instead of replacing it ( GHSA-chm7-fjpm-927x ) What changed: These flags are now always blocked in comment extra args: -chdir , -plugin-dir , -out , -generate-config-out , -state , -state-out , -backup . Before, only -chdir and -plugin-dir were blocked. Flags are matched by name. One entry blocks both the - and -- spellings and the =value form. --blocked-extra-args now adds to the built-in list. Before, setting it replaced the defaults, so an operator could unblock -chdir or -plugin-dir that way. That is no longer possible. Who is affected: Users who pass any of these flags in comments. Watch for atlantis plan -- -generate-config-out=... , which some teams use to generate config for import blocks. Operators who set --blocked-extra-args to allow one of the default flags. Users who pass Terraform's own -state or -backup to atlantis state rm in comments. Those are blocked too. How to tell: the comment is rejected with flag "" is not allowed in extra args . What to do: To use -generate-config-out or the other flags, put them in extra_args of a workflow you control (server-side, or a repo workflow the server allows). Workflow extra_args are not checked. If you listed both spellings in --blocked-extra-args , you can drop the -- entries. Nothing breaks if you leave them. The comment -var-file allowlist covers more commands, spellings and paths ( GHSA-chm7-fjpm-927x ) What changed: --var-file-allowlist (default: --data-dir ) is now enforced on apply , import and state rm , not only plan . It now catches --var-file and values that contain = . Any value containing a .. element is refused, even if it would resolve inside the repository (for example envs/../common.tfvars ). After cloning, repository-relative paths are resolved with symlinks followed. The result must be inside the repository or an allowlisted directory, so a symlink into an allowlisted directory still works. A symlink whose target does not exist is refused. A plain file that doesn't exist yet is still allowed. Only -var-file in comment extra args is checked. Workflow extra_args are not. Who is affected: users who pass -var-file in comments on these commands with a path outside the repository and the allowlist, a path containing .. , or a path that goes through a committed symlink leading outside the repository. How to tell: errors include var file path

is not allowed by the current allowlist: [...] var file path

must not contain '..' elements var file path

resolves to , which is not allowed by the current allowlist: [...] var file path

is a symbolic link whose target does not exist What to do: use a clean path inside the repository, or add the directory to --var-file-allowlist . atlantis state rm now enforces apply and import requirements ( GHSA-cxvq-66x3-pwhw ) What changed: state rm used to skip command requirements entirely. It now has to meet every requirement in the project's apply_requirements plus every one in its import_requirements . There is no separate state_rm_requirements key. Who is affected: servers with state in --allow-commands and projects that set apply_requirements or import_requirements ( approved , mergeable , undiverged , policies_passed ). How to tell: state rm is refused with the usual requirement messages, ending in before running state . For example: Pull request must be approved according to the project's approval rules before running state. What to do: get the PR approved, mergeable, etc. before running state rm , or loosen the requirements for that project. If Atlantis can't fetch the PR status, approved and mergeable count as not met. API GET /api/locks requires X-Atlantis-Token when an API secret is set ( GHSA-xgrg-fpp6-q6fm ) What changed: this endpoint used to be open even with --api-secret set. Web basic auth never covered /api/ paths. Who is affected: scripts and dashboards that call GET /api/locks without a token on servers that have --api-secret set. If no API secret is set, the endpoint stays open. How to tell: HTTP 401 with error code UNAUTHORIZED and message invalid or missing API token . The 401 body uses the newer API error envelope, not the old top-level lock-list body. What to do: add the header X-Atlantis-Token: . paths[].directory is validated on /api/plan and /api/apply ( GHSA-mwfx-fvfc-7q5w ) What changed: non-empty directories have to be clean, repo-relative paths. The request is now rejected for: absolute paths, including a bare / .. that leaves the repository backslashes glob characters * ? [ ] { } Valid values are cleaned: ./dir and dir/ both become dir . An empty directory is still allowed. Who is affected: API callers that send any of these. Before v0.49.0: /modules/vpc ran in modules/vpc but didn't match that directory's atlantis.yaml project, so it ran with default project settings. A bare / meant the repo root. A glob such as envs/* matched configured projects by pattern. The API docs already said globs were unsupported, but the code accepted them. That undocumented behavior is gone. How to tell: HTTP 400 with invalid directory "

": directory must be a clean repo-relative path . What to do: send directories relative to the repo root, with no leading slash. Use . for the repo root. List each project directory explicitly instead of using a glob. VCS GitHub clone URLs must be on the configured GitHub host, and head and base repos must share a host ( GHSA-6mjf-4m52-m5cq ) What changed: For GitHub, the host in the base and head repositories' clone URLs must equal --gh-hostname (default github.com ). The check runs on webhooks, on API plan/apply requests, and when a comment command fetches the pull from GitHub. The comparison ignores case and port. A clone URL with no host is rejected. For every VCS, a command is not run when the PR's head repository is on a different host than its base repository. Who is affected: GitHub Enterprise Server or GHE Cloud setups where --gh-hostname is not the host GitHub puts in clone URLs. For example: an internal alias or IP address, or a reverse-proxy name that differs from the GHES hostname. Any provider whose webhooks report a different host for the head and base repositories (not expected for normal setups). How to tell: GitHub webhooks get HTTP 400 with parsing pull data: ... expected clone url host "" but had "" . Check your webhook deliveries in GitHub for 400s after upgrading. API requests fail validation with failed to parse repository: ... , and comment commands fail with the same host error. The head/base host mismatch is silent on the PR . The server logs head repo host "" does not match base repo host "", not running command at warn level. What to do: set --gh-hostname to the hostname that appears in your repositories' clone URLs. Approval checks use each reviewer's latest review (GitHub, Gitea) ( GHSA-fm5f-jg8p-x2vw ) What changed: for apply_requirements: [approved] (and import_requirements / state rm ), Atlantis now reads every page of reviews and takes each reviewer's most recent approve or request-changes review. GitHub: an approval no longer counts if the same reviewer later requested changes. Dismissed approvals were already ignored. Changes requested by a different reviewer don't cancel someone else's approval. Gitea: an approval no longer counts if it was dismissed, if Gitea marked it stale, or if the same reviewer later requested changes. Gitea marks every review on a PR stale when a push changes the PR's diff, whether or not "Dismiss stale approvals" is enabled in branch protection. A push that doesn't change the diff doesn't. Comment-only reviews still neither grant nor revoke approval. GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps are unchanged. Who is affected: GitHub and Gitea users relying on approved . On Gitea, any push that changes the diff invalidates every existing approval until reviewers approve again. How to tell: apply is refused with Pull request must be approved according to the project's approval rules before running apply. even though an old approval is visible on the PR. What to do: re-approve the PR on its current head. Apply Apply is refused when the plan file differs from the one recorded at plan time ( GHSA-5vwh-xc92-8h64 ) What changed: When a plan stage contains the built-in plan step, Atlantis records a SHA-256 of the plan file with the project's plan status. apply rejects a plan file that no longer matches that hash, and deletes the file. A plan whose built-in plan step leaves no plan file now fails at plan time instead of at apply. The hash is taken after every plan-stage step has finished, so run steps in the plan stage can still post-process the file. Plan stages made only of custom run steps record no hash and are not checked. Plans recorded before the upgrade carry no hash and are still accepted. Who is affected: workflows, pre_workflow_hooks or tooling that rewrite or replace the plan file between atlantis plan and atlantis apply . Workflows whose plan stage includes plan but somehow don't leave the plan file at the expected path. How to tell: Apply fails with plan file for dir "" workspace "" project "

" does not match the plan that was recorded when it was created; run `atlantis plan` . Plan fails with plan step did not write a plan file for dir "" workspace "" project "

" . What to do: run atlantis plan again. Don't modify the plan file after the plan stage finishes. Any post-processing has to happen inside the plan stage, before Atlantis records the hash. Additive: PlanHash is a new field in stored project status and in PlanSuccess API responses. Old stored data decodes unchanged. Setup GitHub App setup flow is bound to the browser that started it ( GHSA-rx6x-hrg2-g435 ) What changed: /github-app/setup now issues a one-time state nonce and an HttpOnly cookie, both valid for 10 minutes. /github-app/exchange-code only accepts a callback that carries both. Only one exchange runs at a time; other requests get 409. More than 16 pending setups get 429. Right after a successful exchange, both pages return 400 ( Atlantis already has GitHub credentials ) in the same process. Before, that only happened after a restart with credentials configured, so record the credentials shown before leaving the page. Who is affected: only operators running the one-time GitHub App setup (no app configured yet). Servers that already have an app configured are not affected. Setup now fails if it is split across browsers, has cookies disabled, takes longer than 10 minutes, or is scripted by calling the exchange URL directly. How to tell: HTTP 400 on the exchange page with GitHub app setup state is not valid for this browser, start again from /github-app/setup or GitHub app setup state expired, start again from /github-app/setup . What to do: reload the setup page and complete the flow in one go, in the same browser. Also pass --web-basic-auth while setting up. Non-breaking fixes GHSA-48vm-qqx3-7w83 : web basic-auth username and password are compared in constant time. Valid and invalid credentials behave as before. GHSA-jxcj-v552-f5q4 : output: hide on custom run and multienv steps now also hides output when the step fails, in both the PR comment and the job message. The multienv parse error no longer echoes the offending line; it now reads like invalid environment variable definition: misquoted at offset 8 . env steps are unchanged. Security fixes Advisory Severity Summary Reported by GHSA-6mjf-4m52-m5cq Critical Clone URL host was not checked against the configured VCS host, so the fork check could be bypassed and untrusted code run. @watsa01 GHSA-56q6-8vmp-v2qm High A later project in a multi-project atlantis.yaml could skip the server's allowed_workflows check. @bcarikci-dev GHSA-5vwh-xc92-8h64 High Apply did not bind to the reviewed plan, so a replaced plan file could be applied under an existing approval. @luantq0 GHSA-9q39-mgw7-5789 High A symlink in a pull request could make Terraform run, or write its plan file, outside the checkout. @zer0d4y5 , @Hama1cco , @avrlab233 , @manus-use GHSA-fm5f-jg8p-x2vw High Dismissed Gitea approvals (and superseded GitHub approvals) still met apply_requirements: [approved] . @danieltk76 GHSA-mwfx-fvfc-7q5w High /api/plan and /api/apply did not validate paths[].directory at the API boundary. (The authentication half was fixed in v0.45.0; constant-time basic auth is GHSA-48vm.) @SnailSploit GHSA-xgrg-fpp6-q6fm High GET /api/locks exposed lock metadata without an API token. @SDSZEHTZ , @hatjwe GHSA-48vm-qqx3-7w83 High Web basic auth credentials were compared in non-constant time. @iaohkut-from-NightWolf-Team GHSA-chm7-fjpm-927x Medium The comment -var-file allowlist could be bypassed, allowing arbitrary file reads on the Atlantis server. @dashingDragon , @arpitjain099 , @kah-ja , @luantq0 , @dead1nfluence GHSA-cxvq-66x3-pwhw Medium atlantis state rm ignored apply and import requirements. @luantq0 GHSA-jxcj-v552-f5q4 Medium output: hide on custom run and multienv steps leaked output into PR comments when the step failed. @bcarikci-dev GHSA-rx6x-hrg2-g435 Low The GitHub App setup callback had no CSRF protection ( state parameter). @geo-chen Thank you to everyone who reported these issues, and to @chenrui333 and @pseudomorph for reviewing every fix. Other changes API: parallel_plan is honored for API plans and drift detection ( #6963 ). GitLab: Atlantis no longer adopts commit pipelines it doesn't own ( #6932 ). Images: Debian curl and openssl pins moved to the trixie-security versions ( #6990 ). Docs: pre- and post-workflow hook pages warn against re-evaluating PR-supplied environment variables, and Command Requirements explains that an approval is not tied to a plan ( #6965 ). CDKTF references now point to CDK Terrain ( #6902 ). Architecture governance and feature lifecycle ADRs proposed ( #6923 ). Highlights 
 Emergency security release for the  eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise . The private keys of eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate certificates were compromised; some of those intermediates are cross-signed by a root that every trust store includes.  We recommend all users upgrade.  
 
  Go 1.27.3:  Atlantis is now built with go1.27.3, whose  crypto/x509  rejects any certificate chain containing the eight compromised keys ( CVE-2026-111943 ). Go does not check revocation, so Atlantis v0.48.1 and earlier, built with go1.27.1, would accept a certificate issued with those keys for any host, including the VCS APIs Atlantis sends credentials to. go1.27.3 also includes the standard library fixes from go1.27.2. 
  Trust store update in the images:   ca-certificates  is updated to Alpine  20261020-r0  and Debian  20250419+deb13u1 . Both remove  emSign ECC Root CA - G3 , and Debian also removes the  Comodo AAA Services root  that cross-signed some of the affected intermediates. This covers the other TLS clients in the image (git, curl, Terraform/OpenTofu and conftest). 
  Runtime image refresh:  Debian curl  8.14.1-2+deb13u7  and openssl  3.5.7-1~deb13u3  security pins, Alpine 3.24.2, Terraform 1.16.5, conftest 0.70.1. 
  Dependency security updates:   golang.org/x/net  v0.60.0 and  vite  v8.3.3. 
 
 If you build Atlantis yourself, rebuild with go1.27.3 or go1.26.10 or later. The  terraform ,  tofu  and  conftest  binaries are built by their own projects; update them when their releases with the Go fix are available.

Atlantis v0.48.0 
  ### Terraform and OpenTofu Binaries Removed from Debian and Alpine Images  
 Starting with Atlantis  v0.49.0 , the Debian- and Alpine-based Docker images will no longer include bundled Terraform or OpenTofu binaries. 
 Users can continue to use Atlantis' automatic binary download functionality to fetch and use the Terraform or OpenTofu versions required by their workflows. 
 This change allows the Atlantis project to focus its security and maintenance efforts on the Atlantis application and its container images, rather than taking responsibility for the security lifecycle, vulnerability management, and distribution of third-party Terraform and OpenTofu binaries. 
 Users who require pre-installed binaries can continue to build custom Atlantis images based on the official images. 
 Highlights 
 
  Safer plan/apply lifecycle.  Atlantis now hashes the loaded apply plan, persists plan results before reporting success, and applies the verified managed-plan snapshot. 
  New slim container images.  Alpine and Debian slim images are available without bundled Terraform or OpenTofu, for deployments that provide their own tooling. 
  Terraform and runtime compatibility.  End-of-life Terraform versions without security support were removed from the standard images. The bundled versions, Debian and Alpine bases, Go toolchain, OpenTofu, Conftest, and Git LFS were refreshed. 
  Operational and security hardening.  GitLab webhook tokens are omitted from errors, and drainer and workflow-hook status handling is more reliable. The  GHSA-rjh2-4xgw-p2hj  shell-injection fix is retained from the mainline history; it was already shipped in v0.47.1 and is not presented as new here. 
  Documentation and localization.  Spanish documentation and translation infrastructure were expanded. 
 
 Runtime and compatibility changes 
 
 Standard images now use Terraform 1.16.3 and 1.15.9, with older unsupported Terraform versions removed. 
 Alpine and Debian base images were updated, along with the Go 1.27.1 runtime/toolchain, OpenTofu 1.12.6, Conftest 0.70.0, and Git LFS 3.8.0. 
 New  alpine-slim  and  debian-slim  image targets do not bundle Terraform or OpenTofu.

Highlights 
 
  OpenTofu .tofu support : Atlantis now detects OpenTofu versions from .tofu and .tofu.json files, includes those files in default autoplan and project discovery behavior, and detects Terraform Cloud/Enterprise workspace configuration from .tf.json, .tofu, and .tofu.json projects. 
  Broader core workflow coverage : The E2E harness now activates expanded fixtures from  runatlantis/atlantis-tests#21001 , covering multi-project targeting, autodiscovery, configured JSON projects, custom workflow environment behavior, and long-output status contexts. 
  Safer plan/apply behavior : This release hardens apply validation against stale head/base plan state, preserves on_apply locks during plan cleanup, and fixes /api/plan with policy checks enabled while preserving per-project /api/apply behavior. 
 
 Project Health 
 
  Top-Ranking Atlantis Issues 📊  Maintainers and contributors can now use  #6608  to see open Atlantis issues ranked by community thumbs-up reactions. The ranking is a signal for prioritization and contribution, not a roadmap commitment or acceptance guarantee. 
 Atlantis now uploads Go coverage to GitHub Code Quality, lints the separate e2e Go module, and has automated top-issue ranking to make maintenance work more visible. 
 We welcome contributors across bug reports, focused fixes, documentation improvements, issue reproduction, and issue moderation/triage. 
 
 Call For Adopters 
 If your organization uses Atlantis and can share a sanitized setup or adoption note,  runatlantis/examples  is a good place to contribute it. Public examples help users learn from real deployments, help the project document its ecosystem, and can become future candidates for atlantis-tests fixture coverage. 
 What's Next 
 We are also looking at flag lifecycle improvements so Atlantis has a clearer path for introducing, documenting, deprecating, and eventually removing server flags.

This minor release adds alpha drift detection and remediation APIs, new localization and automerge controls, notification improvements, and several provider and execution fixes. 
 Highlights 
 
 Added alpha drift detection, status, remediation, remediation history, and drift webhook APIs. These APIs are alpha and their request/response behavior may change in future releases. ( #6360 ) 
 Added runtime localization support with built-in English and Spanish catalogs plus custom YAML overrides. ( #6506 ) 
 Added automerge controls for default merge method and disabling automerge labels. ( #6573 ,  #6593 ) 
 Improved GitHub team allowlists to honor team hierarchy. ( #6365 ) 
 
 Alpha: Drift detection and remediation APIs 
 
 Added alpha drift detection APIs, drift status API, drift remediation API, and remediation history/result read endpoints. ( #6360 ) 
 Added drift webhook notifications, including Slack and HTTP webhook support. ( #6360 ) 
 Added  --enable-drift-detection  for drift detection/status/history behavior. 
 Added  --enable-drift-remediation  for destructive remediation apply. 
 Drift APIs require API authentication with  X-Atlantis-Token  and repository allowlist authorization. 
 Remediation  action:"apply"  requires cached positive drift with  has_drift:true  for the same repo/ref/base branch/project/path/workspace. 
 Drift API inputs include ref, path, workspace, repository, and allowlist safety validation. 
 Operators should test carefully before production use, especially with hooks, policy checks, allowlists, multi-project repos, and custom workflows. 
 
 Features 
 
 Added  --language  and  --language-config-file  to localize Atlantis pull request comments and override language catalog strings. ( #6506 ) 
 Added  --automerge-method  to set a default merge method for automerging, currently implemented for GitHub. ( #6573 ) 
 Added  --disable-automerge-label  to disable automerge label behavior. ( #6593 ) 
 Extended  autodiscover.ignore_paths  to targeted  -d  commands. ( #6466 ) 
 Streamed project failure text to the job page. ( #6414 ) 
 
 Fixes 
 
 Scoped regex project plans correctly when  --restrict-file-list  is enabled. ( #6598 ) 
 Detected OpenTofu versions using the project distribution. ( #6597 ) 
 Re-downloaded Terraform/OpenTofu binaries when the existing binary appears invalid. ( #6454 ) 
 Unified Terraform/Terragrunt project directory detection, including  .tf ,  .tf.json , and  terragrunt.hcl  indicators. ( #6455 ) 
 Hardened path handling for CWE-22 path-expression issues. ( #6254 ) 
 Preserved Docker healthcheck port fallback behavior. ( #6588 ) 
 Clarified status-update logging when no URL is available. ( #6595 ) 
 
 Provider fixes 
 
 Bitbucket Cloud: validate pagination next URLs before following them. ( #6260 ) 
 GitHub: only apply GitHub App checkout behavior to GitHub repositories. ( #6119 ) 
 GitHub: support child-team inheritance for  GH_TEAM_ALLOWLIST . ( #6365 ) 
 
 Notifications and webhooks 
 
 Slack notifications now show the pull request head branch instead of the base branch. ( #6316 ) 
 Slack notifications can include the pull request description. ( #6540 ) 
 Documentation now clarifies Slack payload fields and GitHub team hierarchy behavior. ( #6596 )

This patch release focuses on provider correctness, safer apply behavior, plan/output rendering fixes, and refreshed runtime foundations. 
 Highlights 
 
 Broader GitHub Enterprise support: existing GitHub Enterprise Server behavior is preserved, and GitHub Enterprise Cloud  *.ghe.com  tenants now use the correct REST and GraphQL API endpoint patterns. 
 The Debian-based Atlantis image now uses Debian 13 Trixie with refreshed pinned system packages including curl, git, OpenSSH, GnuPG, OpenSSL, and libcap. 
 Apply safety is improved by failing closed when apply-lock backends cannot be reached and by correctly evaluating pull request status for API apply requirements. 
 Mergeability and status behavior is more accurate across GitHub, GitLab, GitHub App checkout flows, and no-change apply statuses. 
 Terraform/OpenTofu plan output rendering now handles  to forget , multi-unit summaries, heredoc/multiline-string diffs, and very long single-line command output more reliably. 
 
 Provider fixes 
 
 GitHub: support GitHub Enterprise Cloud  *.ghe.com  API URL patterns. ( #6339 ) 
 GitHub: truncate status contexts to GitHub's 255-character limit. ( #6541 ) 
 GitHub App: skip unused source remotes on fork-safe checkout paths. ( #6568 ) 
 GitLab: filter mergeability status checks by the merge request ref/SHA. ( #6557 ) 
 GitLab: scope project apply mergeability to the project being applied. ( #6543 ) 
 Azure DevOps: guard nil pull request status values while parsing pull events. ( #6496 ) 
 Gitea: avoid nil response dereferences while logging API errors. ( #6442 ) 
 
 Apply, plan, and output fixes 
 
 Fail closed when the apply lock backend cannot be reached instead of allowing applies to proceed on lock-check errors. ( #6533 ) 
 Populate pull request status before API apply requirement evaluation so  approved  and  mergeable  are enforced correctly. ( #6535 ) 
 Show no-change plans as  up to date  in apply statuses instead of implying they were applied. ( #6498 ) 
 Preserve and aggregate  to forget  plan statistics. ( #6570 ) 
 Aggregate multi-unit plan summaries correctly. ( #6490 ) 
 Remove stale  .tfplan  files when refreshing a working directory to a new ref. ( #6358 ) 
 Skip non-git directories when finding pending plans. ( #6453 ) 
 Preserve command output lines longer than 64 KiB. ( #6544 ) 
 Color changed lines inside heredoc and multiline-string diffs. ( #6561 ) 
 Fix a divergence check order issue. ( #6452 ) 
 
 Runtime and maintenance 
 
 Updated the Debian image base to Debian 13 Trixie. ( #6572 ) 
 Updated OpenTofu and CI/test image digests. ( #6549 ,  #6580 ,  #6581 ) 
 Removed the obsolete  check-lint  Makefile target. ( #6554 ) 
 Pinned scorecard-related Go and npm commands for OpenSSF compliance. ( #6480 ) 
 Updated website and CI dependencies, including security-related frontend dependency updates. ( #6563 ,  #6564 ,  #6565 ,  #6566 ) 
 
 Documentation 
 
 Clarified GitHub App merge checkout behavior. ( #6577 ) 
 Clarified recent status, locking, VCS, pending-plan, and output-handling behavior. ( #6578 ,  #6582 )
